evidence: New imports in rich/progress.py:1-5 are stdlib only (io, mmap, os, sys, warnings). The existing relative imports (progress.py:42-51) are unchanged.
The reader depends only on io, typing and the Progress public methods (`advance`/`update`, progress.py:130, 165). Nothing new is imported from other rich modules.
The module has no `__all__` (base rich/progress.py contains none), and there is no plugin or column registry that the feature needs to join.

The file-object interface is implemented by subclassing io.RawIOBase and BinaryIO (progress.py:104) and by the context-manager protocol (progress.py:198-209 for the reader, 211-236 for the context wrapper). The reference uses the same approach (reference progress.py:171, 263).

No third-party dependency is added. typing_extensions is used only in the Python<3.8 fallback (progress.py:38-40), and pyproject.toml:30 already declares `typing-extensions ... python = "<3.9"`. The reference uses the same fallback.

Reader logic (progress accounting for read/readline/readlines/readinto/seek) lives in `_ProgressFileReader` (progress.py:104-209). Display lifecycle (start/stop around the reader's enter/exit) lives in `_ProgressFileContext` (progress.py:211-236). Module-level functions only assemble these pieces (progress.py:306-345 `_file_progress`, 347-470 `open`/`wrap_file`).

Shared Progress construction is factored once into `_file_progress` (progress.py:306-345). The reference duplicates that column/Progress block in both `wrap_file` and `open` (reference progress.py:377-400, 504-527). The candidate's factoring is a valid alternative with no behavioural difference.
Logic for the Progress methods stays in the Progress class (progress.py:1172-1320), which is where the reference puts it.

Progress tracking goes through existing Progress APIs: `add_task` (progress.py:1525), `update` and `advance` (progress.py:1352, 1446), `start`/`stop` (progress.py:1099, 1104). The candidate does not add a parallel progress mechanism.
Text decoding is delegated to the stdlib io.TextIOWrapper (progress.py:1270-1273), the same choice as the reference (reference progress.py:1270-1276).

`_ProgressFileReader` touches the Progress only through its public `advance` and `update` methods (progress.py:130, 165). Access to `self._tasks` and `self._lock` happens inside Progress.wrap_file (progress.py:1306-1311), so the Progress internals stay inside the class.

Ownership is respected: `owns_handle` decides whether close() closes the underlying file (progress.py:136-141). The caller-owned wrap_file path leaves the file open (progress.py:1280-1320; tests/test_progress.py:691-703).
